title: Clostridioides difficile recurrence
bottleneck: C. difficile infection recurs in 20 to 30% of patients after initial treatment, and in over 40% after a first recurrence, because antibiotics that treat it also devastate the protective gut microbiota. Recurrent disease causes severe colitis and significant mortality in the elderly.
why_it_blocks: It is the paradigmatic disease of microbiome disruption, a direct consequence of antibiotic use, and standard antibiotics perpetuate the cycle.
current_state: Fecal microbiota transplantation and approved live biotherapeutic products, a non-traditional approach of the kind WHO's pipeline analysis tracks, have transformed recurrent C. diff care, but standardized, scalable, safe products and prevention strategies are still maturing. Narrow-spectrum antibiotics and microbiome-sparing approaches could prevent C. difficile in the first place, but they face the same broken development economics as other antibacterials. Prevention through stewardship remains the most cost-effective lever.
